A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. All 32 pages of v1 and 36 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable and support comparison. Algorithms, theorems and proofs can be matched across renaming and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports algorithms, theoretical guarantees and proofs, but no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis results.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical and explicitly identifies empirical validation as future work. Its introductory runtime comparison is attributed to Zhang et al. (2023), not experiments conducted by this work.

M1.justification: DOCLO is renamed DROCULO, but its updates, communication, infeasible projection and feedback transformations are retained. The explicit case-specific query formulas and additional BQM pseudocode describe existing constructions. Two-point estimation is discussed as a possible alternative rather than incorporated into the proposed algorithms.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or conducts training or evaluation on test scenarios. The added power-network example in v2 is motivation, not an evaluated application.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparison methods. Table 1 retains the earlier theoretical comparators; its added DOBGA row summarizes a method and guarantees already compared in v1 Section 2.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an experimental evaluation protocol. The retained block-size, step-size and smoothing schedules are analytical algorithm parameters, not changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, error analyses or evaluated case studies. The new concavity appendix supplies mathematical reasoning rather than supplementary experimental analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Expectations and bounded stochastic-oracle assumptions remain part of the theoretical analysis.

E6.justification: Theorems 1–6 retain their reported regret, communication and linear-oracle complexity rates and parameter ranges. There are no empirical result entries. DOBGA's newly tabulated rates already appeared in v1 Section 2.

T1.justification: New Appendix A defines linear assignments, proves a characterization of concavity and gives an equivalent characterization of upper-linearizability. v2 also explicitly states compactness and specialized smoothness/oracle assumptions and ties Theorems 3–6 to named function cases. The central regret bounds and their proofs remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The main framework, novelty and regret-tradeoff claims remain. However, v2 corrects the introductory comparison: v1 says theta=1 matches Liao et al.; v2 correctly associates theta=1/2 with DPOBGA and theta=1 with DOBGA's regret, consistent with the tabulated rates.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation and applicability discussion: network disconnection prevents global agreement, approximation ratios are distinguished as optimal or conjectured, and one-point versus exact two-point feedback is discussed. It also explains block averaging's variance role and explicitly identifies empirical validation as outstanding.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents T mod K=0 and specifies underlying oracle Q interfaces and case-specific query points in the feedback pseudocode. Parameter schedules remain unchanged. A documentation drawback is that Algorithms 4–5 use z without an explicit sampling step, although its distributions remain available in Appendix B.

R1.justification: v2 adds a substantive decentralized online convex optimization survey, including Lee et al. and Wan et al., and connects the framework to Pedramfar et al. (2025) on uniform wrappers. It also adds approximation-hardness and gradient-estimator literature while removing several earlier background citations, substantially revising the surrounding research discussion.

P1.justification: The introduction and contribution list are extensively rewritten. Preliminaries are reorganized into notation, function classes, problem formulation and set oracles; algorithm and analysis sections are combined; feedback extensions are organized by function cases. Explanations expand throughout, and DOCLO becomes DROCULO.

P2.justification: Four feedback algorithm displays move from the appendices into main Section 5, substantially reorganizing the layout. Table 1 gains method names, a DOBGA row and an expanded explanatory caption. v2 also adds a BQM algorithm display and publication headers; these changes exceed simple renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the existing theory easier to assess through explicit assumptions, clearer oracle explanations, accessible feedback pseudocode and the new concavity proof. It also resolves the introductory tradeoff-comparison inconsistency and acknowledges the lack of empirical validation. These gains outweigh limited documentation regressions, particularly the implicit z sampling in Algorithms 4–5, but leave the central algorithms and guarantees largely unchanged.
